## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `temporally-anchored-graph-proximity`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-08-04T05:54:30.594Z.

Catalog entry (27) — temporally anchored graph proximity.

Extends the catalog. Entries 1 through 26 stand unchanged and none is restated. Entries 1 through 24 score a candidate against the query. Entry 25 scores it against what this session has already been served. Entry 26 scores it against how often its defect family has recurred. Entry 27 scores it against the graph as it stood at the moment the query is about, which is not the graph that exists now.

The signal. Every relationship edge in this tracker carries a creation timestamp, and coverage is exactly 100 percent over all 9,152 authored rows, verified this session by direct census of the item files rather than through a graph command. Nothing in the scoring pipeline reads that timestamp. Every graph-derived feature the engine can currently compute, degree, centrality, path distance, community membership, dominance, slack, is computed against the HEAD snapshot only.

Why HEAD is the wrong graph for a large class of queries. On this corpus 7,863 of 9,152 edges, 86 percent, were authored during 2026-07, in a backfill campaign. An item closed in April therefore looks far better connected today than it was on the day the work happened. Any relevance score that uses graph position as a proxy for importance is, for every historical query, reading a property the item acquired after the fact. The engine confidently ranks on a signal that did not exist when the thing it ranks was true. This is not noise that averages out; it is a monotone distortion that grows with the distance between the query anchor and now.

The scoring rule. Give every query a temporal anchor. For forward-looking intents, next work, current blockers, what to claim, the anchor is now and entry 27 degenerates to the present behaviour, which is correct. For retrospective intents, why did this break, what shipped in that release, what did this incident touch, what was blocking us then, the anchor is the timestamp the query is about, taken from a named release, an incident window, an explicit selector, or the anchor of the item under examination.

Then weight each edge by the distance between its assertion time and the anchor rather than treating all edges as equally present. Two regimes, one function. Edges asserted after the anchor are evidence about the future of the anchor and are discounted toward zero for reconstruction intents, because including them is exactly the leakage described above. Edges asserted before the anchor are discounted by age with a half-life, so that a relationship asserted the week before the anchor outweighs one asserted a year earlier, which encodes the ordinary fact that recent structure is more explanatory of a moment than ancient structure.

The same function serves the forward case with the anchor set to now, where it does useful work rather than degenerating: it damps the influence of very old edges on present recommendations, which is the graph-side analogue of the recency signal entries 1 through 24 already apply to item fields. One implementation, both regimes, selected by the anchor alone.

Interaction with the existing catalog. Entry 26 conditions on recurrence, and recurrence is measured over history, so entry 26 is only sound when the edges it counts are the edges that existed at each occurrence. Entry 27 is therefore a precondition for 26 being correct rather than merely a companion to it. Against entry 25, session novelty, the two are orthogonal and compose by multiplication. Against the ordering signals, an as-of blocker set is what makes the question of how long a chain actually held answerable at all, since at HEAD every resolved chain is simply absent.

Cost and bounding. The naive implementation replays history per query and is not viable at the scales this engine targets. The tractable form is a time-indexed projection of the durable graph index keyed by assertion time, so that an as-of edge set is a range scan rather than a reconstruction, with replay reserved for anchors older than the retained index horizon and for verification. The budget contract is unchanged: an as-of scoring pass inherits the same row and token bounds as its HEAD equivalent, and the cost receipt separates index cost from replay cost so a caller can see which regime it paid for. Entry 27 is unimplementable until the projection it needs exists, which is the feature filed this session as pm-3yzyfe, and that item is the correct dependency to carry.

Falsifiable claim, so this entry can be retired if wrong. On this corpus, ranking the same retrospective query at HEAD and at its anchor must produce materially different orderings. If the two orderings agree within noise, the backfill did not distort historical position and entry 27 buys nothing but cost. The measurement is cheap and should be taken before the scoring change is built, not after.

Scope clarification from individual-ownership review: pm-3yzyfe owns a related measurement, read primitive or defect fix. It does not independently deliver this proposed ranking behavior. Reuse its evidence and public API; evaluate the additional behavior in this experiment.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
